title: Lists and virtualisation
summary: FlatList and SectionList: keys, windowed rendering, getItemLayout, pagination with onEndReached and the props that keep long lists smooth.

sections.title: Why not map in a ScrollView?
sections.body: `ScrollView` renders every child up front. For 1,000 rows that means 1,000 sets of native views, slow startup and high memory. `FlatList` virtualises: it renders the rows near the viewport, measures them and replaces far-off rows with blank space.

sections.title: FlatList basics
sections.body: Pass `data`, `renderItem` and `keyExtractor`. Keys must be stable and unique, just like keys in `map`. If items have an `id`, return it as a string.
sections.code:
<FlatList
  data={orders}
  keyExtractor={order => order.id}
  renderItem={({ item }) => <OrderRow order={item} />}
  onEndReached={loadMore}
  onEndReachedThreshold={0.5}
  ListEmptyComponent={<Text>No orders yet</Text>}
  refreshing={refreshing}
  onRefresh={refresh}
/>

sections.title: The rendering window
sections.body:
`initialNumToRender` sets the first batch. `windowSize` is measured in viewport heights: the default `21` keeps 10 screens above and 10 below the visible one. `maxToRenderPerBatch` limits work per frame. Smaller windows save memory but show blank areas on fast scrolls.

If every row has a known, fixed height, give `getItemLayout`. The list can then compute any row's offset as `index * height` without measuring, which makes `scrollToIndex` reliable and skips layout work.
sections.code:
const ROW = 72
<FlatList getItemLayout={(_, index) => ({ length: ROW, offset: ROW * index, index })} />

sections.title: Sections, pagination and re-rendering
sections.body:
`SectionList` takes `sections: [{ title, data }]` and adds `renderSectionHeader` and sticky headers.

`onEndReached` fires when the user scrolls within `onEndReachedThreshold` (in visible lengths) of the end. It can fire more than once, so guard against loading the same page twice.

`FlatList` is a `PureComponent`: it only re-renders rows when `data` changes identity. If a row depends on other state, pass it in `extraData`.

Exercises here run as TypeScript in a browser sandbox with no React Native runtime, so they model this logic as plain functions and reducers. The same functions drop straight into a real app: call them from a component, a hook or a store.

pitfalls: Using the array index as the key when rows can be inserted or removed.
Calling `loadMore` from `onEndReached` without a loading guard, fetching a page twice.
Mutating the `data` array in place, so the list never re-renders.
Nesting a vertical `FlatList` inside a vertical `ScrollView`, which disables virtualisation.

gotchas.question: Rows are 50 dp tall and the list is scrolled to offset 1,000. With `getItemLayout`, which index is at the top of the viewport?
A row shows a selected state from `selectedId` in the parent, but tapping does not update it. Why?
gotchas.answer: `FlatList` only re-renders when its props change shallowly. `data` did not change, so pass `extraData={selectedId}`.

gotchas.question: What unit is `windowSize` in?
gotchas.answer: Viewport lengths, not items. `21` means the visible screen plus 10 above and 10 below.
